environment: Apple M4 / Darwin arm64 / Go 1.27.3 / GOMAXPROCS4
implementation: Only len(Merges)==0 bypasses Pieces. Fill a bounded 256-byte local scratch buffer, then count and allocate exactly the remaining emitted bytes only if a 257th valid byte occurs. Negative/out-of-vocabulary IDs and BOS/EOS still emit nothing. Returned strings own their data. No unsafe conversion, mutable global cache or executor policy change. Merged/BPE Decode remains the existing packed-table plus append implementation.
reference: packedTokenizerDecode is the frozen Decode loop using the prior packed Pieces implementation, not the original 257-allocation table. Decode-only generation uses the same model, generateInput, tokenizer wrapper type and sampler on both sides; only its Decode method chooses this reference or production.

selected_microbenchmark.interpretation: Short valid-byte decode is much faster in this microfixture and allocated bytes fall, unlike the preceding Pieces-only change. Benchmark blocks are not randomized paired trials. The all-invalid case is slower despite eliminating allocation. Do not claim a universal Decode speedup or extrapolate the microfixture multiplier to generation.

rejected_experiments.name: single preallocated heap byte buffer
rejected_experiments.reason: Fast for dense long IDs but allocates by input length even when almost all IDs are invalid. The selected scratch/spill path prioritizes bounded small-output storage and exact spill allocation; it is not fastest in every case.

rejected_experiments.name: exact strings.Builder output
rejected_experiments.reason: One allocation alone did not imply faster CPU execution. Rejected as the general solution.

rejected_experiments.name: exact builder for all BPE outputs
rejected_experiments.reason: Reduced output allocation and helped large expansions, but regressed byte-heavy BPE input. Keep the merged/BPE production path unchanged rather than infer a universal benefit or tune a threshold from these fixtures.

decode_only_generation_bench.interpretation: Same-runtime decode-only wrapper comparison for 128 generated tokens. Wrapper/helper overhead differs from prior BenchmarkOwnedGenerate receipts, so compare these rows only to each other. Roughly seven logical objects and 7 KB disappear in the byte fixture; do not assign the previous 255-object Pieces reduction to this change.

generation.interpretation: Three independent processes, byte and merged controls, five shapes each, balanced alternating order and 24 paired trials. Every completion matches outside timing. These are synthetic greedy-sampling fixtures; no self/self temporal controls or real-model throughput study. Byte-process medians change direction. Merged controls include approximately +2.7% despite unchanged merged arithmetic. No established end-to-end latency win or uniform no-regression claim.

verification: Allocation regression fails before Decode modification and passes afterward
Raw bytes, empty/special/invalid IDs, nested and maximum-length merges match the packed reference
Output ownership, concurrent calls and 255/256/257 spill boundaries with sparse IDs
Complete normal and race-enabled Go suites
go vet, isolated offline probe builds, CGO-disabled production build and CLI smoke
decision: Keep the byte-only fast path as the next promising scoped speed/allocation candidate. Preserve generic BPE behavior and all rejected/unfavorable data. Production runtime stays monolithic. No commit, push, PR or merge performed for this local prototype.
